WS03 S8-B: crash-park. DESIGN ONLY, revision 8, made against branch model-plane (S8-A is built: commits c6a95ae0 .. 6ddfae42, ledger entry dfd1a8d5; HEAD was dfd1a8d5 when the design started and is 72c51bc3 now, the two later commits being documentation and evidence only, so the build base is whatever HEAD is when S8B-0 starts, recorded by the lead). `git status --short` shows only the untracked .plan-work/. Model Plane paths are under "apps/Model Plane"; every citation is a function or constant name, never a line number.

S8-B is: the session-core recovery worker PARKS an ACTIVE fold (a run whose executor crashed mid-loop) at its 15-minute recovery deadline instead of ending the run outcome_unknown, so that a resume through the S8-A park route (POST /continue with an empty approval_id and a claim token, AgentResume.mode "park") can continue it.

It changes three crates and nothing else: mp-contracts, session-core and execution-core, plus the compose file, the docs, the DB-test harness script and its contract test, the execution-core contract tests, and an owner-visible CI workflow change. There is NO migration, NO proto change, NO new wire token and NO model-gateway, BFF or SPA change: a crash-parked fold is an ordinary kind=park fold to the S8-A claim, the S8-A resume and the S8-A gateway regime, and RunDetail already projects park_reason crash_interrupted (it is in ParkReason::ALL).

S8-B v1 covers ONE class of run, on purpose: a pinned, root, persistent, read-only (plan_mode and autonomy rung read_only), built-in-tools-only run. That is not a small or empty set: it is every ChatGPT-subscription "Do" turn from the SPA (a subscription turn sends tools [], and the gateway maps plan_mode to the read_only rung) in a non-Space thread of an org with no registered MCP tool, and every API caller that sends a pinned plan_mode run with no client tools; validate_run_route refuses a pinned run without plan_mode unless the effects switch is on. It delivers nothing until something calls the resume route (open_questions). Everything else keeps the committed ~15 minute outcome_unknown. Extending it to effect-capable runs is listed as an owner decision with what it would need, not designed here.

Three design-review rounds (v2, v3 and v4 of the S8 design) each found a critical or high defect in the crash-park half. This revision answers the five that were named, concretely and without the machinery that produced new defects in v4: no thread watermark and no migration, no loop_checkpoint_superseded token, no heartbeat change, no claim grace, no third writer_gate.
summary:
WHAT IT DOES
- The executor, behind its own default-off switch EXECUTION_LOOP_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED, writes ONE eligibility marker, the extension key crash_parkable whose value carries the route model, the connection id, the child ceiling and the parks count a resume needs, on every ROUND-BOUNDARY fold of a run that is crash-resumable AT REST. The S8-A park keys (parks, route_model, route_connection_id, child_ceiling) stay exclusive to park folds: session-core's re-seal derives them from the marker's payload. The marker is computed from facts of the run, never from a tool listing alone, and is re-checked by a pure function shared with session-core (mp_contracts::crash_park::crash_reseal), so the two sides cannot disagree about what a resumable fold is.
- session-core, behind its own default-off switch SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED (effective only with park recovery on), runs one new branch in recover_claimed_terminalization, after the approval check and before the S8-A park spare (which stays the single spare call and hands the obligation back): an active, marked, clean boundary fold of a run that never raised an approval and reserved no ledger row is re-sealed in place under seq+1 as kind=park, state=parked, park_reason crash_interrupted, due at once, and the run's obligation is handed back at the crash horizon. Everything else is terminalized exactly as committed.
- A crash park is held for its own, shorter TTL (SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_TTL_SECONDS, default 3600, clamp 60 s to 30 days), not the park TTL, and the worker reads it whenever park recovery is active, so a crash park nothing resumes costs at most that long AFTER the 15-minute deadline (deadline plus TTL in all, not the TTL alone), not 24 hours, even after the crash switch is killed.
- Resume is the S8-A path, unchanged. A crash-parked fold passes check_park_fold by construction (and a test proves it).

THE ANSWERS TO THE FIVE DEFECTS
1. A crash park nothing can resume is held for the TTL: the marker means "park-resumable at rest". It is written only for a root, pinned, persistent, Space-less, read-only run whose offered tool names are derivable from the tools the loop really runs under (a direct name proof over ctx.allowlist, in addition to the request-kind fact) and which holds no release and was started fresh or by a park resume. An approval continuation (segment or in place), a delegated loop, a client- or MCP-tool run, an unpinned run, a ZDR or waived run never carries it. A deploy or config drift between crash and resume is the one residual: it costs at most the crash TTL.
2. A live-but-silent loop crash-parked under itself, two loops, two answers: the acts of a read-only loop that cannot be taken back are ending the run (its answer and its terminal receipt) and raising an approval, and those are fenced EXACTLY. A loop silent past the 900 s deadline also holds a dead 300 s session bearer by default, so its session-core writes are refused before any seq is compared; the design does not rely on that, it treats a Denied save as 'cannot prove ownership' and stops once the loop's own heartbeat age says the worker may have acted. Before the acts of a marked loop that nothing can take back, ending the run (append its answer and write the terminal receipt, for ANY outcome) and raising an approval, the loop saves a TOMBSTONE fold ("answering" or "paused") through the fenced writer; if that save finds the seq moved (the worker re-sealed, a resume fenced), the run ended, or the save cannot be confirmed (a transient failure: a late append cannot be recalled), the loop stops and does neither; so does a Denied answer (what a loop silent past its 300 s session bearer gets) once the loop's own heartbeat age is at the window. One funnel covers every exit that reaches finalize, typed failures included. The one thing it resolves with its own clock is a Denied answer (the expired-bearer zombie, whose append, and receipt with the same bearer, cannot land either): the loop proceeds only while its bearer is verifiably expired and the last heartbeat the store accepted was sent less than 780 s ago (the larger of its monotonic and wall-clock age), because the worker cannot act before 900 s have passed. A transient failure of the tombstone is NOT resolved by the window: the window bounds when finalize starts, not when its append lands. The worker and the save take the same runs row lock and then the fold row lock, so either the tombstone commits first (the worker then sees a non-resumable fold and does not park) or the re-seal commits first (the tombstone save is stale and the loop never appends). Nothing depends on a clock, on the messages table or on append_message_in_tx's locks. A marked loop also stops at its next loop top after a definitive ownership failure (Stale, Closed, NotFound), and, whatever its writer's state, once a marked fold may be stored and its own last accepted heartbeat is at the window (it must not heartbeat then), so a superseded loop does not burn the rest of its budget.
3. The duplicate-answer guard and the two clocks: there is no clock comparison anywhere. messages.created_at (application clock) is never read; the guard is the ordering of the tombstone save and the append, serialized by the fold row's seq compare-and-set.
4. An old session-core with a new executor: the executor's marker keys are inert extension keys and its tombstone is an ordinary valid fold, so an old store stores them and never crash-parks. A session-core with S8-B and an executor without it sees unmarked folds and terminalizes as committed. Neither direction needs a handshake, because the marker is the executor's opt-in and the store's re-seal refuses any fold without it.
5. The kill and rollback order: crash-park off first (session-core), then the executor's marking, then the S8-A order; session-core below S8-B only after crash parks have drained; an executor below S8-A never while crash parks exist. Each is a row of the failure matrix.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE
- No effect-capable run is crash-parked (a crash makes their effects unknowable; only a read-only run provably has none).
- No thread notice is built in v1 (the question is the owner's, listed).
- No automatic resume and no UI button: crash-park is only worth flipping once something calls the resume route (owner decision, listed with the prerequisites).
- No SPA change: a crash-parked run stays 'running' for the deadline plus the crash TTL and sends no run_parked frame (the executor is dead), so the SPA follows it as waiting, settles 'unknown' after its own fixed 15 minutes and shows a waiting tail again on each reload. An SPA change that recognises a crash park is listed as a prerequisite the owner may set for the session-core switch.

SWITCHES (all default off, strict "true")
- EXECUTION_LOOP_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED (execution-core): marks eligible folds, saves the answering or paused tombstone before ending a run or raising an approval, stops a loop that cannot prove ownership. This is NOT an observation-only flip: a marked loop that finds the run ended (cancelled, terminalized by the worker, a duplicate dispatch) now stops without its late answer or receipt, where committed code appended it (for a run that may have a marked fold stored; a direct first-round answer behaves as committed); a marked loop whose bearers expired but whose last heartbeat is recent keeps the committed immediate failed receipt; a marked loop that cannot confirm its tombstone at run end (a degraded session-core) stops instead of answering and leaves the run to the worker. Owner-gated like the session-core switch. Needs the S8-A resume switches (EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED, EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED, EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED); it does NOT need EXECUTION_LOOP_PARKING_ENABLED. It is also gated by a const (CRASH_RETIRE_BUILT) that stays false until the tombstone step has landed, so an image between the two steps cannot mark by configuration.
- SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED (session-core): the worker's crash-park. Effective only when park_recovery_active() is true.
- SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_TTL_SECONDS (session-core): the wait of a crash park.

Proposed flip order (the owner's call, open_questions): the S8-A flips (1) to (3) with the S8-A park resume live-proven, the executor switch (owner-gated, its visible effects listed), then session-core's, last and owner-gated. Kill order is the reverse.

0. READ THIS FIRST: WHAT THE TREE IS (verified at HEAD dfd1a8d5)

session-core
- loop_checkpoint::save locks the run (run_owner_tx, runs FOR UPDATE) and then the fold row (FOR UPDATE), compares seq (a mismatch is aborted "loop_checkpoint_stale", a closed row failed_precondition "loop_checkpoint_closed", an ended run "loop_checkpoint_run_ended"), seals under AAD seq and upserts. Park rules (validate_park_save, park_accepted) apply only under park_recovery_active(). It refuses park_reason crash_interrupted ("park_reason_reserved"); that stays.
- loop_checkpoint::claim with an empty pause_ref and park_recovery_active() runs CLAIM_PARK_SQL: kind='park', state 'parked' or 'resuming' under a lapsed lease, park_until <= now(); it never sets updated_at. A held lease of any token is claim_held; not due is park_not_due.
- terminalization::recover_claimed_terminalization takes lock_run_status (runs FOR UPDATE) and lock_managed_obligation (FOR UPDATE), checks the lease, a terminal run (supersede), has_pending_approval, then (S8-A) spare_parked_run (PARK_SPARE_HORIZON_SQL takes the fold row FOR UPDATE and spares a kind=park fold, parked or resuming, until updated_at + park TTL, handing the obligation back at LEAST(that, now + 900 s)), then PARK_HELD_SQL, then apply_managed_terminal_outcome (outcome_unknown, one receipt, the fold purged in the same transaction).
- heartbeat_managed_run_inner (runs, then the obligation) renews state 'open' and deadline_at = Utc::now() + 900 s for an open or processing obligation; it answers already_terminal for a terminal run. It is NOT touched by S8-B.
- run_loop_checkpoints (0047): one row per run, kind in round|pre_effect|pause|park, state in active|paused|parked|resuming|closed, seq, pause_ref, park_reason, park_until, authority_digest, segment_no, ciphertext, fold_digest, claim_token_hash, claim_expires_at, updated_at (the park's age and the TTL anchor).
- session_tool_audit_intents (0013 + 0048): (run_id, action_id) rows with status reserved|completed|failed|not_run|unknown_outcome and reserved_at; the executor reserves only effectful calls and a release (agent.rs, `entry.class.is_effectful() || is_release`).
- approvals (0003) has run_id and an index on it; a pinned run never gets a pause fold (resume::run_pause_mode returns "" for a non-empty provider_hint), so its approval is a cold one and the fold stays whatever the last round saved.
- the delegated bearers a run carries (session, inference, data plane) live 300 s by default (run_budget.rs; PLANE_TOKEN_TTL_* overrides), and a pinned run stops starting rounds 60 s before the earliest expires. The executor's heartbeat and its terminal receipt use fresh service tokens (session_terminal_auth.rs, terminal_tokens), NOT those bearers; fold saves, AppendMessage and every other session-core call of the loop use the delegated session bearer, so a loop that outlives it gets Unauthenticated on all of them (classify_status: Refused(Denied)) except those two.
- execution-core installs no metrics recorder (fold.rs record_metrics says so): its counters are no-ops today and its info! lines are the evidence. session-core installs a Prometheus recorder.
- the descriptor cipher is built on demand with DescriptorCipher::from_env() (the recovery worker has none today); seal and open take an AAD scope, scope_aad(run, org, user, seq).

execution-core
- run_rounds: the ONE writer_gate; the loop top checks ctx.route.is_stopped(), the latched refusal (park site A), the deadline (park site B), then heartbeat_managed_agent_run(..).await? (any heartbeat error aborts the loop with Err, before finalize). A round's fold is saved best effort at the END of a round that ran tools (folds.save_round); a round that ends in an answer saves nothing. An effectful root call is preceded by folds.save_pre_effect (fail closed: Stale, Closed, Refused, Unavailable all HOLD the effect). FoldWriter::apply moves Stale and Closed to State::Failed and the loop goes on.
- finalize: when !req.zdr && refusal.is_none() it appends the assistant message (append_message), then record_managed_agent_terminal_outcome. Two RPCs.
- fold.rs: build_fold writes only extension effect_ledger; Snapshot is the loop's locals; FoldWriter::{seeded,new,save_round,save_pre_effect,save_fence,save_park,pause_fold}; save_tombstone_as is private; Header::tombstone makes a fold with no conversation and extension not_resumable.
- park.rs (S8-A): StaticFacts / run_parkable (includes parking_active()), ParkStop, try_park, park_fold (the ONLY writer of EXT_PARKS, EXT_ROUTE_MODEL, EXT_ROUTE_CONNECTION, EXT_CHILD_CEILING, pinned by park_writer_violations), is_park_resume, admit, derivable_tool_defs, claim_parked, check_park_fold (14 rules), route_request, fence_parked.
- agent.rs: offered_tools decides derivability by REQUEST KIND (a request with a resume is never derivable; a fresh one is derivable when nothing a caller or an MCP server added is in the set and the server-resolved view was read); run_agent_with_route_parkable sets LoopContext.tools_derivable = derivable && no release, builds the allowlist from the tools the loop really runs under (after a continuation's snapshot replaced them), and park_continuation gives a park resume the derived set.
- The permission pre-pass in run_rounds rejects, at EVERY depth, a call whose rung the run was not granted (permission::check_autonomy_rung) and, in plan mode, a risky call; effect_class_of derives from the same permission::rung_required_for, so a run granted read_only cannot run a call the ledger classes as effectful. A delegated loop (depth > 0) has no fold writer.
- model-gateway: an executor Err(Aborted) or Err(Unavailable without a connect-phase io error) is neither a confirmed rejection nor "never reached", so a fresh run's stream answers agent_dispatch_unavailable plus RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and terminalizes nothing; a park continue goes through park_dispatch_of and never terminalizes.

1. THE DESIGN IN ONE PAGE

(a) ELIGIBILITY AT REST (executor, marker). On every boundary fold a marked run writes, the executor adds ONE extension key, crash_parkable, whose value is {v:1, model, connection_id, child_ceiling, parks}: the identifiers a resume needs, content-free. It does not write the S8-A park keys (parks, route_model, route_connection_id, child_ceiling): those stay exclusive to park_fold, which keeps S8-A's guard on them untouched, and crash_reseal derives them from the payload. A fold is "at a boundary" when round_in_flight is None and pending is None; a pre_effect fold of an open round, a pause fold and a park fold never carry the marker. The marker is written only when ALL of these hold at that save: crash_marking_active() (the switch, the const CRASH_RETIRE_BUILT, and the resume half: park_resume_built() && park_resume_active()), the S8-A static facts minus the parking switch (depth 0, not zdr, not waived, no Space, tools_derivable by request kind, holds no release, seed Fresh or Parked, pinned, connection id and model present, restated as run_crash_parkable's own conjunct list, never by splitting run_parkable), the run is READ-ONLY (req.plan_mode and the autonomy rung is read_only), the tool NAMES the loop really runs under are derivable (ctx.allowlist EQUALS the names of base_tool_defs(false), or those plus the one server-resolved name tickets.create: exactly the set a resume derives, because a resume requires its derived names to equal the fold's), a round is left (rounds_executed + delegated_rounds < max_rounds, the budget the resume will use) and the run is under the park cap (parks_so_far < MAX_PARKS_PER_RUN). Because it is written at each boundary save, a budget that has run out removes it by itself.

A marked loop also fences a VISIBLE call for the one purpose of removing the marker: a root round that contains a plan.* call (plan.propose writes a plan the user can approve, and is classed Read) or a subagent.* call (it records child runs) first saves the open-round pre_effect fold through save_pre_effect, but only while the writer is Active. The calls are held ONLY when the writer has lost ownership (lost_ownership(), after the attempt): a transient save failure, or a writer that failed for another reason (Refused(KeyUnavailable | Unimplemented), a store that is off), does NOT hold them, because committed code never holds a Read-classed call and a fence must not take plan.propose or a delegation away from a run that has no crash park to protect; they are dispatched as committed code dispatches them (fail open). An open-round fold is never marked, so after a SUCCESSFUL fence a crash after such a call finds an unmarked fold and the run is terminalized as committed; the next end-of-round fold is marked again. After a failed (fail-open) fence a crash parks the marked boundary before the call and a resume repeats it: a second plan proposal (the newest wins) or a second delegation record, benign and listed in the risks. The ledger is not involved. This costs coverage on purpose: a crash inside a delegation round (the longest rounds) or a plan-proposing round is not parkable.

(b) ONE PURE DECISION, TWO CALLERS (mp-contracts). mp_contracts::crash_park::crash_reseal(fold, run_id) -> Result<LoopFoldV1, CrashRefusal> is the only code that decides whether an active fold may become a crash park and what the parked fold is. It refuses (closed tokens, metric labels): a tombstone (not_resumable, which includes the answering and paused tombstones), no marker or a malformed one (strict parse: v 1, non-empty model and connection id, ceiling >= 1), ledger off in the fold, no system prompt first, an open round, a pending pause, a Space, an unpinned authority, a plan_mode that is false or a rung that is not read_only, a payload park count at the cap, a missing prompt digest, another run's fold (run_mismatch). It does NOT recompute the round budget (the constants live in execution-core): the marker's presence guarantees a round was left when it was written, and the oracle test pins that at the boundary. It returns the fold with pending = Park{park_ref(run, parks+1)} (no step, call or fingerprint), the S8-A park keys set from the marker's payload (route_model, route_connection_id, child_ceiling, and parks = payload parks + 1) and the marker removed. session-core calls it in production; execution-core calls it in the oracle test that proves "a marked fold re-seals into a fold check_park_fold accepts".

(c) THE WORKER'S CRASH PARK (session-core). In recover_claimed_terminalization, after the approval check and BEFORE the S8-A spare (which stays the one and only spare call: for a fold that is already a park the crash branch refuses at its state check before it opens any ciphertext, and for a re-sealed fold the same spare statement then hands the obligation back), when crash_park_active(): crash_park_run(tx, cipher, run_id) runs inside the transaction that already holds the run row and the obligation row, then takes the fold row FOR UPDATE. It refuses (the run is terminalized as committed) unless: the run is persistent; a fold exists, is state 'active' and kind round or pre_effect (a park-resume fence is a pre_effect fold with no open round, so the check is by content, not by kind); a cipher is available and opens the fold under AAD seq; check_fold and the row's authority_digest agree with the fold; crash_reseal accepts it; the run has NO row in session_tool_audit_intents (a read-only run reserves nothing, so any row is an anomaly) and NO row in approvals (a read-only run that ever raised an approval is not a run that merely crashed: its fold is stale by construction, and a pinned run saves no pause fold to say so). On success it re-seals under seq+1, kind='park', state='parked', pause_ref = the new park_ref, park_reason 'crash_interrupted', park_until = now() (due at once), a fresh fold_digest, claim fields cleared, updated_at = now() (the TTL anchor), writes the content-free CHECKPOINT_SAVED event like a park save, and the caller hands the obligation back through the S8-A spare at the crash horizon. No terminal state is written.

(d) THE RETIRE FENCE AND THE OWNERSHIP STOP (executor). A marked (armed) loop is about to do one of two things nobody can take back: END THE RUN (finalize: append its answer when retention and the outcome allow it, then write the terminal receipt with a fresh service token) or RAISE AN APPROVAL (pause_for_approval). Immediately before either it calls retire_fence, which uses FoldWriter::retire(counters, authority, reason): one save of a tombstone fold (kind round, extension not_resumable with the closed word "answering" or "paused", no conversation, built from the header alone) at the expected seq, through the same save path as every fold (so the one stale-after-ambiguous probe applies). retire_fence returns Ok at once for a loop that is not armed (its first statement), so an unmarked loop behaves exactly as committed at both sites. There are exactly TWO call sites. (1) One exit funnel in run_rounds: every outcome the loop hands to finalize passes it (Answered, Concluded, Exhausted, OutOfTime, InferFailed with or without a typed refusal, RouteUnavailable), whatever branch produced it: the body after the writer is built becomes an `async` block (a `return` or `?` inside it leaves the block), and the funnel after it passes Err, Paused and Parked through untouched and fences everything else. (2) The pending-pause block: the FIRST statement inside `if let Some(pending) = pending_pause.filter(..)`, before `let offered` and before folds.pause_fold( (a PauseFold holds the writer mutably until pause_for_approval consumes it, so nothing can be placed between the two), with reason "paused".

The decision. (0) The fence exists to keep a MARKED fold from being crash-parked, so it applies only while one may be stored: the writer tracks that (FoldWriter::marked_fold_may_be_stored(): a save that carried the marker and returned Ok or ambiguous sets it, an Ok save that did not carry it clears it (a NotAccepted park, which stores the loop's own unmarked park row, too), an ambiguous one leaves it, a writer that never saved has it false). A run that answers in its first round, or whose last stored fold is unmarked (budget spent, a visible-call round's open-round pre_effect fold, an Ok tombstone), has none: for such a writer that has not lost ownership retire_fence returns Ok at once, with no RPC, no wait and no stop, because no crash park can exist for it. Otherwise the loop proceeds past retire_fence only when it holds a committed tombstone or a reason why none can matter; everything else stops. (1) Ok (the tombstone committed): proceed. From that commit on no crash park can ever be created for the run, whatever the transport does later. (2) A writer that has failed with Stale, Closed or NotFound (FoldWriter::lost_ownership), or a tombstone save answered Stale, Closed (which includes run_ended: classify_status folds it) or NotFound (the seq moved, the run ended, the run is gone), is POSITIVE evidence that another writer or the run's end got there first: STOP at any age. The stop is Err(Refusal::ContinueInProgress.status()) (Aborted "continue_in_progress", an existing closed token, never a confirmed rejection), returned before finalize and before the approval exists: no append, no receipt, no approval. (3) Anything the save could not CONFIRM stops too, at ANY age: Unavailable or a timeout (after the one retry of (5)) and a ContentRefused (refused, not committed: a local credential-shape or size refusal, or a server InvalidArgument or OutOfRange). A Stale that follows an ambiguous attempt is NOT in this list: it is resolved inside save_bytes by the shared one-shot probe at expected+1, which matches the loop's own earlier commit and returns Ok (proceed: the tombstone is stored), or is Stale too (the stored seq is at least expected+2: a foreign writer) and is the definitive stop of (2). The reason is that a delayed request cannot be recalled: the window of (4) bounds when finalize STARTS, not when its append LANDS, so one partition that fails the tombstone can also hang the append until after a crash park was resumed, and a late answer would then be a second one. The price is stated, not hidden: a session-core outage at the exact moment a marked loop ends costs that run its answer (committed code would also have lost it unless the store came back inside the append's own failure), and the run is left to the worker: crash-parked and resumable if the tombstone did not land, outcome_unknown at the deadline if it did. A stop is never a duplicate. The exception is a store that answers disabled or Unimplemented, a missing descriptor key, or a run the store reports as not persistent (NotPersistent): the writer goes Off or Failed for a non-ownership reason, nothing was written, and this replica cannot write; the loop proceeds as committed (R19b). (4) Denied (Unauthenticated or PermissionDenied; for a loop silent past its 300 s session bearer that is the ordinary answer, because the bearer is checked before the seq), or a writer already Failed with it (FoldWriter::ownership_unproven), is the one UNPROVEN case, and it is resolved only when the session bearer is VERIFIABLY EXPIRED (run_budget::bearer_expiry of the session bearer plus the verifier's 30 s leeway at or before the current epoch second, the two pure helpers RunDeadline already uses; an unreadable exp counts as not expired): a Denied answer from a bearer that is not expired is not explained by expiry (a verifier or authorization hiccup, the earlier blip of R19g), so it is treated as unconfirmed and STOPS. For an expired bearer it is resolved with the executor's OWN CLOCK: the loop remembers when it last SENT a heartbeat that the store accepted (the run-level heartbeat before run_rounds, then each loop-top heartbeat; a heartbeat error already ends the loop) as a BeatMark that holds BOTH an Instant and a SystemTime, and its age is the LARGER of the two elapsed times (so a host or VM suspend, which stops the monotonic clock but not the wall clock, can only lengthen it). The worker cannot crash-park a run before its obligation's deadline_at, which is the heartbeat's receipt time plus 900 s, and the receipt is never earlier than the send, so while that age is under the age window (900 s minus a 120 s skew margin, constants in mp-contracts pinned to session-core's MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS) no crash park can exist and no resume can be running, and the append that follows is refused by the same expired bearer, so nothing can land late: the loop proceeds and writes the committed immediate failed receipt. At or past the window it stops. (5) retire's transient retry is ONE retry (two attempts, 100 ms apart, only for Unavailable and only while is_active() still holds) with the gated 10 s timeout, not the 2 s round timeout (a must-confirm save is not a best-effort one), so a degraded store costs a run end up to about 30 s before the stop (typically about 20 s for two Unavailable answers, 2 x 10 s plus 100 ms; the probe adds up to 10 s only after a slow Stale). So a superseded loop silent past the deadline always stops, whatever the transport does, and a healthy loop whose bearers expired a moment ago still writes its immediate failed receipt as committed code does. At every loop top, before anything else (before the route-stopped, latched-refusal and deadline checks and before the heartbeat), an armed loop stops when its writer has lost ownership, or when a marked fold may be stored and its own last accepted heartbeat is at or past the window, WHATEVER its writer's state: a loop silent that long must not heartbeat, because the worker may already have crash-parked the run, and a zombie's heartbeat would renew that park's obligation and reset its own age (round 5: a zombie whose in-flight end-of-round save returned Ok after a host suspend, with a monotonic-clock deadline that did not fire, could otherwise refresh its mark, reach the funnel with a young age and finalize over the crash park). 2. WHY THE SAFETY ARGUMENT IS EXACT (the part v4 did not have)

What can a read-only marked loop A do that anyone can see? It cannot run an effect: the rung gate rejects every call the ledger classes as effectful, at every depth, and plan mode rejects risky calls. It can read, infer, spend subscription quota, publish informational events, write a plan proposal (plan.propose is classed Read, writes a plan the user can approve, and is superseded by the next proposal) and delegation records (subagent.*), and do the acts nobody can take back: end the run (an appended answer and the terminal receipt) and raise an approval (the only calls a read-only run can still be gated on are the disclosure-consent read, read_subagent_result, which asks on every posture, and a read a capability policy chooses to ask about; a pinned run's approval is cold). So duplicate EFFECTS are impossible by construction; the two visible writes that are not effects (a plan proposal, a delegation) are fenced by the pre_effect fold of section 1(a): a crash after one finds an unmarked fold, and a stale loop's save for it is refused so the call is held; and the acts that matter, ending the run and raising an approval, are fenced by the retire tombstone.

Let R be the commit of A's tombstone save (before it ends the run or raises an approval) and P the commit of the worker's re-seal. Both are transactions that take the runs row lock first (run_owner_tx in save, lock_run_status in the worker) and then the fold row lock, so they are totally ordered.
- If P < R: A's tombstone save expects the old seq, finds seq+1 and answers aborted "loop_checkpoint_stale" (or closed/run_ended if the run ended): A stops and appends, receipts and raises nothing. The one exception is the stale-after-ambiguous probe: a loop whose EARLIER save timed out has one retry at seq+1, and that can match the re-sealed seq. Then A wins the compare-and-set against a resume that has not fenced yet, A owns the run again (the park is undone) and the resume's fence is the stale one. Either way exactly one of A and B proceeds, because both are saves at the same seq.
- If R < P: the worker reads a tombstone: crash_reseal refuses (not_resumable). The run is terminalized as committed. A's append, receipt or approval happens after R, so it can only land on a run that is never crash-parked.
Therefore: if A appends an answer, writes a receipt or raises an approval, the fold was already a tombstone, and the run is never crash-parked afterwards; if the run is crash-parked, neither ever happens from A. A crash after the append and before the receipt leaves a tombstone, so the worker terminalizes (outcome_unknown, as committed) and nothing resumes a run that already answered.

The second, independent fact: a loop silent for 900 s holds session, inference and data-plane bearers that expired at 300 s (by default). Every session-core write it can still try is refused Unauthenticated before any seq is compared, which the loop reads as Refused(Denied). That is why a Denied answer cannot be read as 'not stale', and why the funnel resolves it with the age rule: a zombie silent past the deadline has a last accepted heartbeat older than 900 s, so it stops; its terminal receipt uses a fresh service token (so does its heartbeat), so WITHOUT the funnel a zombie that failed typed (InferFailed, RouteUnavailable) would have terminalized the crash park through the service token while B ran. With a PLANE_TOKEN_TTL longer than the deadline the bearers do not expire and the seq compare-and-set is what stops it. The age rule is the third: it uses no store answer at all, only the executor's own clock, at the exit funnel it covers the Denied answer only (a transport failure of the tombstone stops the loop by itself: an unconfirmed tombstone never proceeds, at any age), and at the loop top it stops a silent armed loop that may have a stored marked fold before it can heartbeat. The design needs all of them and relies on none alone.

The residual is stated, not hidden, and it is narrow. (i) An unconfirmed tombstone never proceeds, for a run that may have a marked fold stored (the others make no tombstone call): a healthy loop that cannot reach session-core at its end STOPS instead of risking a late append (round-4 high finding: the earlier fail-open design let one partition fail the tombstone and hang the append past a resume). That is a cost, not a duplicate: the answer in the loop's memory is lost and the run is left to the worker. (ii) A writer that cannot write at all (Off, or Failed for a non-ownership reason such as KeyUnavailable) cannot tombstone: the loop finalizes as committed, so on a replica set whose configuration disagrees a marked fold stored earlier can be parked by another replica (R19b); with a delayed append that is a duplicate path, closed only by the drain-before-rolling rule. (iii) A Denied tombstone from a verifiably expired bearer with a recent heartbeat proceeds: no crash park can exist yet, and the append with the same expired bearer cannot land. The exact belt for (ii) and for any unforeseen late append is a durable fact ordered with the append: an idempotent final answer per run (a unique partial index on the final assistant message per thread and run, with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in append_message_in_tx) or the v4 thread watermark; both need a migration, neither is built, both are listed for the owner.

A loop that is alive but silent for 15 minutes and is crash-parked while it works: it can no longer fold-save, it stops at its next loop top, before its heartbeat (its own last accepted heartbeat is older than the window and a marked fold may be stored), so it neither renews the park's obligation nor resets its own age; it can neither end the run nor raise an approval (the tombstone is refused, Stale or Denied). It may waste read-only work. A depth-1 child of such a loop can still heartbeat the root run's obligation, which is harmless because the fold is a park and the spare handles it (R19d). A live loop that DOES heartbeat in time is not parked at all: a heartbeat between the worker's claim and its recovery transaction turns the obligation back to 'open', and the worker's existing check (state must still be 'processing' with its own lease) abandons the pass.

3. THE FIVE DEFECTS, ONE BY ONE

(1) UNRESUMABLE RUNS HELD FOR THE TTL.
Cause in v2 to v4: the marker was set from a tool listing, or from the request of a continuation, so a client-tool run, an approval continuation, or a run whose snapshot tools came from a pause could carry it.
Now: (i) marked only if crash_marking_active() and the static facts hold, which include tools_derivable by REQUEST KIND (offered_tools never calls a resume request derivable, and run_agent_with_route_parkable ands it with "no release"), seed Fresh or Parked and no release: three independent facts that each exclude an approval continuation, segment or in place; (ii) NEW: the tool names are proven from the loop's own allowlist, which is built AFTER a continuation's snapshot replaced the request's tools, so even a future code path that let a continuation through the first three facts would fail here when its snapshot held a client or MCP tool; (iii) the re-seal is refused without the marker, and crash_reseal re-derives every structural fact check_park_fold needs except the round budget (which the marker's write condition guarantees and the oracle test pins at the boundary); (iv) the oracle test builds a marked fold, re-seals it and runs check_park_fold on it; (v) the residual (deploy or config drift between crash and resume: prompt digest, tool names, a route that no longer resolves) is bounded by the deadline plus the crash TTL, not the park TTL; (vi) an unmarked fold is terminalized at the committed deadline, which a DB test pins for each excluded class. What is excluded, honestly: every SPA turn that sends client tool specs, every run in an org with an MCP tool, every effect-capable run.

(2) A LIVE-BUT-SILENT LOOP PARKED UNDER ITSELF: see section 2. The four facts the review named: save_round is best effort (a marked loop reads lost_ownership at the next loop top and stops); a stale save only fails the writer (it now also ends a marked loop); the heartbeat ignores already_terminal (the funnel's Closed covers an ended run, so the loop never appends to one or writes its receipt; the heartbeat is left alone); append_message_in_tx locks only threads (nothing waits on it: the append is ordered AFTER the tombstone by the fold row, and the worker never queries messages). A zombie raising an approval card, or terminalizing the run through its service-token receipt after a typed failure, is fenced the same way: the funnel stands before finalize, not before the append.

(3) THE CLOCKS: no comparison of messages.created_at (Utc::now() in append_message_in_tx) with run_loop_checkpoints.updated_at (database now()) anywhere. The one place two timestamps meet is none: the worker uses no timestamp at all in its decision (the ledger and approval facts are "any row", not "after the fold"), and the park's due time and TTL are database now() on both sides.

(4) OLD SESSION-CORE, NEW EXECUTOR: section 1(d) and the failure matrix. The executor learns nothing from the store; it writes data an old store ignores. The tombstone save is a valid fold save an old store accepts, and an old store has no crash park, so nothing can resume a run behind the tombstone. A store without S8-B never re-seals. The reverse (S8-B store, executor without marks) never re-seals either. There is no coupled flip to get wrong.

(5) THE KILL AND ROLLBACK ORDER: section 6.

invariants: A crash park is created by exactly one function, crash_park_run, inside the worker's transaction that holds the run row, the obligation row and then the fold row, and only for an ACTIVE fold of a persistent run whose content passes crash_reseal, which has no row in session_tool_audit_intents and no row in approvals.

mp_contracts::crash_park::crash_reseal is the only decision of what an eligible fold is and what the parked fold is. session-core calls it; the executor's oracle test calls it and then check_park_fold on the result.

The executor writes the marker (one key, crash_parkable, a CrashMark payload) only on a boundary fold (round None, pending None), only when crash_marking_active() and run_crash_parkable and a round is left and parks < MAX hold. A park fold, a pause fold and a pre_effect fold of an open round never carry it. The S8-A park keys stay exclusive to park_fold. With the switch off or CRASH_RETIRE_BUILT false every fold is byte-identical to S8-A's.

The marker's tool fact is computed from the allowlist the loop really runs under (built after a continuation's snapshot replaced the request's tools: it EQUALS the base names or the base names plus tickets.create), in addition to the request-kind fact, the seed kind and the release fact. An approval continuation (segment or in place), a delegated loop, a client-tool or MCP-tool run, a Space run, a ZDR or waived run, an unpinned run, a run with plan_mode false or any rung but read_only never carries the marker and is terminalized at the committed deadline.

A read-only marked run cannot run an effect at any depth: effect_class_of and check_autonomy_rung share rung_required_for. A round that contains a plan.* or subagent.* call is preceded by a pre_effect fold (unmarked, with an open round) for a marked loop, so, after a SUCCESSFUL fence, a crash inside that round is never parked and a stale loop's call is held; after a failed (fail-open) fence a crash may park the marked boundary before the call and a resume repeats it (R13).

A marked (armed) loop ends the run (finalize: the answer append and the terminal receipt, for ANY outcome including typed failures) or raises an approval only after retire_fence returned Ok, or in one of these cases: (0) no marked fold may be stored for the run (FoldWriter::marked_fold_may_be_stored() is false: a run that answers in its first round, or whose last stored fold is unmarked), so no crash park can exist and nothing needs fencing; (a) its writer is not Active, has not lost ownership and is not unproven (a NotAccepted park the loop itself closed, a store that is off or answers Unimplemented, a missing descriptor key, a writer failed for another non-ownership reason: R19b); or (b) the only answer was Denied, or the writer is already Failed(Denied), AND the session bearer is verifiably expired, AND the loop's own last accepted heartbeat was SENT less than the age window ago (900 s minus 120 s), by the larger of its monotonic and wall-clock age. A tombstone that is not confirmed (Unavailable or a timeout after the one retry, ContentRefused) stops the loop at ANY age, as do Stale, Closed, run_ended and NotFound, a writer that lost ownership, and a Denied at or past the window or with a bearer that is not verifiably expired: Aborted continue_in_progress, before finalize or the approval: no append, no receipt, no approval. An unarmed loop is untouched. retire_fence has exactly two call sites.
A tombstone is a fold no resume restores (is_resumable() false) and crash_reseal refuses it (NotResumable).

Of one run's tombstone save and one crash-park re-seal exactly one takes effect, because both take the runs row lock and then the fold row lock. If the tombstone commits first the run is never crash-parked afterwards; if the re-seal commits first the loop never ends the run or raises an approval, except that a loop whose earlier save was ambiguous may take the run back through its one probe, in which case the resume's fence is the stale one: exactly one proceeds.

No clock, no messages row and no thread lock enters the crash-park decision. messages.created_at and run_loop_checkpoints.updated_at are never compared; the park's due time and its TTL are database now() on both sides.

An armed loop stops at its next loop top, before the heartbeat and before any inference, when park::must_stop says so: its writer has lost ownership (Stale, Closed or NotFound), or a marked fold may be stored and park::beat_age(&last_beat) is at or past the age window, whatever the writer's state (a loop silent that long must not heartbeat). The status it returns is an existing closed token, Aborted, which the gateway never treats as a confirmed rejection, so no stream of a superseded loop terminalizes the run. A writer the executor itself turned off after a NotAccepted park, whose own row it closed (Off(SelfClosed)), has lost nothing and finalizes as committed. A marked loop with a stored marked fold NEVER closes a row it did not write: after an ambiguous park save it does not close expected+1 (that seq may hold the worker's crash park) and keeps its writer Active, so the funnel settles ownership.

A crash park is kind park, state parked, park_reason crash_interrupted, due at once (park_until = now()), anchored at updated_at, with parks incremented by exactly one, the S8-A park keys set from the marker's payload and the marker removed. The executor never writes crash_interrupted and the save RPC still refuses it (park_reason_reserved) while park recovery is active (validate_park_save runs only under park_recovery_active(); with park recovery off a crash_interrupted park row would be stored as an ordinary parked row, which is S8-A's own exposure, restated here).

A crash park is spared until updated_at + SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_TTL_SECONDS, which is itself reached only after the 15-minute deadline (bound whenever park recovery is active, whatever the crash switch says) and then terminalized once through the unchanged outcome_unknown path; a typed park keeps the park TTL. Crash parking writes no terminal state and no receipt.
The worker never takes the threads row, a messages row, an approvals row or a ledger row lock for crash parking. The lock order is runs, obligation, fold.
With SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED off, park recovery off or the store off, the worker, the heartbeat and the claim are byte-identical to S8-A's (a source pin and a DB control).

The resume of a crash park is the S8-A resume, unchanged: the claim by the empty reference, check_park_fold, route_request, the fence at the claimed seq. The resumed loop is itself marked (seed Parked) and shares the park cap of 5 with typed parks.
Cancel, the TTL and any terminal transition purge a crash park exactly as they purge a typed park.
S8-B adds no proto field, no migration, no closed token, and changes no model-gateway, BFF or SPA source. run_parkable, StaticFacts and park_fold keep their text.
CRASH_RETIRE_BUILT is false until the retire fence is built, so an image cannot mark by configuration without the fence.
A ZDR or waived run never gets a marker and never gets a crash park: the executor's facts exclude it, the worker's retention check refuses it, and the store_proofs Park entry names the tests.

Logs, metrics, events and the tombstone's reason are ids, counts and closed words only (answering, paused, the CrashRefusal labels, the site words); no conversation, tool argument or credential reaches them.
failure_matrix: F1 The executor of an eligible run crashes after a round fold, all switches on, no approval: at the deadline the worker re-seals the fold (seq+1, park, crash_interrupted, due now), the obligation is spared at the crash horizon, RunDetail shows resumable with park_reason crash_interrupted; a park continue claims it, the executor fences, the loop continues, ONE answer is appended and the run completes.
F2 The same crash before any fold exists (round 1): no fold, the committed worker ends the run outcome_unknown at the deadline.

F3 The executor crashes after the retire tombstone, before or after the append: the fold is a tombstone, crash_reseal refuses (NotResumable), the worker terminalizes outcome_unknown as committed (the answer may be on the thread, as committed). Nothing resumes a run that had already answered.

F4 A marked loop pauses for the disclosure-consent read: the tombstone 'paused' is saved before the approval exists; the approval spares the run while pending; when it resolves or expires the run ends as committed (S8-0 on: outcome_unknown), never crash-parked, because the stale boundary fold is gone. If the 'paused' tombstone could not be confirmed the loop stops before raising the approval (F29), except for a Denied answer from a verifiably expired bearer with a recent heartbeat, where crash_park_run's approvals fact still refuses the run.

F5 An eligible loop A is alive but silent past 15 minutes and is crash-parked. A's session bearer (300 s by default) is dead: its next fold save or retire is Unauthenticated (Denied); with a long-lived bearer it is Stale. A's own last accepted heartbeat is older than 900 s, so the age rule applies: a Denied answer or an unproven writer STOPS the loop (the age is past the window), and so does any transport failure of the tombstone (an unconfirmed tombstone never proceeds, at any age); a Stale, Closed or NotFound answer stops it at any age. A returns Aborted continue_in_progress at its next loop top (a silent armed loop with a stored marked fold stops there by age alone, before it can heartbeat, whatever its writer's state) or at its exit funnel, before any append, receipt or approval; a typed failure (InferFailed, RouteUnavailable) is stopped by the same funnel and writes NO receipt, so the crash park is not terminalized by A's service-token receipt, even when every RPC of the woken loop fails at the transport. A later continue (B) re-infers from the parked fold and answers once.

F6 The same A heartbeats at the right moment: a heartbeat between the worker's claim and its recovery transaction returns the obligation to open, the worker's lease check abandons the pass, the fold stays active, nothing is parked.

F7 A's tombstone save and the worker's re-seal race: the runs row lock orders them. Tombstone first: the worker refuses (not_resumable), terminalizes, A appends after its own save (a run the worker is ending: committed behaviour). Re-seal first: A's save is stale (or its one probe wins the compare-and-set, then A owns the run and a resume's fence is the stale one). Never both an answer and a live crash park.

F8 An approval continuation (segment or in place), a delegated loop, a Space, ZDR, waived, unpinned, client-tool or MCP-tool run, an effect-capable run (plan_mode false or a rung above read_only): never marked; crash_reseal would refuse them anyway; terminalized at the committed deadline.
F9 A marked run crashes with a row in session_tool_audit_intents or in approvals: refused (ledger_not_empty, approval_exists), terminalized as committed.

F10 A deploy or config drift between crash and resume (prompt digest, tool names, research switch, server-resolved view, an image skew between crash_reseal and check_park_fold): the first continue closes the fold (park_not_restorable) and the run ends at the renewed deadline; if nobody continues, the crash TTL ends it (outcome_unknown), SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_TTL_SECONDS (default 3600) after the re-seal, which itself happens at the 15-minute deadline: 75 minutes after the last heartbeat by default.
F11 A continue whose route no longer resolves: park_route_unavailable, no close, no default route (S8-A); the lease lapses; the crash TTL ends it.

F12 The gateway park form, the BFF flag, an image below S8-7 or S8-8, an executor resume switch, or the GATEWAY's own AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED or EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED (the committed S7 rollback turns the gateway off first) is off while crash parks exist: the continue is refused (continue_disabled, not_resumable or a 400); the parks are held for the crash TTL and then end outcome_unknown. The kill order forbids turning them off first.

F13 OLD session-core (below S8-B) with a NEW executor, marking on: folds carry an inert extension key, the tombstone is an ordinary valid fold the store accepts, and no crash park ever exists. The run differs from committed in: one extra RPC at its end, a pre_effect save before plan and delegation rounds, and the ownership stop (a run cancelled or ended under the loop, or a store that refuses it, ends the loop without a late answer or receipt; a duplicate dispatch's loser stops). These are flip (5)'s visible effects, owner-gated.
F14 NEW session-core with crash park on and an OLD executor (below S8-B, or marking off): the folds carry no marker, crash_reseal refuses (NotMarked), every run is terminalized as committed.

F15 SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED off, park recovery off or the store off with eligible folds: the committed worker; existing crash parks are still spared (park recovery on) until the CRASH TTL (not the park TTL) and are claimable; with park recovery off each is terminalized within 15 minutes and a continue gets not_resumable.

F16 The descriptor key is missing in the worker (DescriptorCipher::from_env fails): Refused(key_unavailable), terminalized as committed. A fold sealed under another AAD: Refused(did_not_authenticate), terminalized.

F17 Two session-core replicas pick the same overdue run: SKIP LOCKED and the lease let one in; if both reach the fold, the second finds a park (spared) and not an active fold. Replicas of different images (S8-A and S8-B) decide per obligation: an S8-A replica spares a crash park under the park TTL; drain before a rolling deploy.
F18 The worker's transaction fails or session-core restarts mid re-seal: it rolls back, the obligation lease lapses after 60 s, the pass is retried; no partial park exists.

F19 Cancel while crash-parked: cancelled, the fold purged and RUN_CANCELLED in one transaction; the obligation is superseded on the next pass; a later continue is not_resumable. Cancel of a LIVE marked run (one that may have a marked fold stored; a direct first-round answer appends as committed): the loop's next save or its funnel gets run_ended (Closed) and it stops with no late answer or receipt (committed: it appends after the cancel): visible effect of flip (5).

F20 The crash TTL passes (the deadline plus the TTL after the last heartbeat): one outcome_unknown terminal through the unchanged path, the fold purged, mp_session_managed_parks_expired_total{reason=crash}. A typed park of another run keeps the park TTL.

F21 The resumed loop B crashes after its fence: its fold is a marked boundary fold again (fence fold, seed Parked, payload parks carried); the worker parks it again; at five parks (typed and crash together) the next crash is terminalized.
F22 A crash park is claimed (state resuming) and B dies before its fence: the lease lapses after 120 s and the park can be claimed again; the S8-A spare keeps it until the crash TTL.

F23 The retire save fails Unavailable or times out (the one retry too) for a healthy loop that may have a marked fold stored, with a recent heartbeat: the loop STOPS (Aborted continue_in_progress): no append, no receipt, no approval. The tombstone may or may not have committed: if it did, the worker later terminalizes the run outcome_unknown (the answer in the loop's memory is lost); if it did not, the marked fold is crash-parked at the deadline and a resume answers once. Cost: a degraded session-core at run end costs the run its answer, after up to about 30 s of waiting. No append was sent, so no late-delivered append can duplicate.

F24 The retire save is answered Stale, Closed or run_ended: the loop returns Aborted continue_in_progress at any heartbeat age. Answered NotFound (the run row is gone) it stops at any age; answered Unauthenticated or PermissionDenied it proceeds only when the session bearer is verifiably expired and the heartbeat age is under the age window (a healthy loop whose bearers just expired writes the committed immediate failed receipt) and stops otherwise (an old age, or a bearer that is not expired: a verifier or authorization hiccup). A stop: a fresh run's stream answers agent_dispatch_unavailable plus RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED and terminalizes nothing; a park continue stream gets a park_continue continue_in_progress frame through park_dispatch_of and nothing is terminalized.
F25 An UNMARKED loop (switch off, ineligible run) meets a stale save: unchanged, the writer fails and holds effects, the loop goes on and finalizes as committed.

F26 The last allowed round: the boundary fold after it carries no marker (no round left), so a crash then is terminalized; a resume of an earlier park with one round left is marked until that round is spent.

F27 EXECUTION_LOOP_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED is turned off, or execution-core or model-gateway restarts or is deployed, while (5) and (6) are on: a switch is container environment, so flipping it recreates the executor and every in-flight loop dies; the gateway drains in-flight turns for MODEL_GATEWAY_DRAIN_SECS (120 s) before it exits and its RunAgent task is spawned, so only a hard kill or a turn longer than the drain drops the call and the executor's handler future with it; an executor recreate has no drain (SIGTERM ends main and the handler is awaited inline), so every in-flight loop dies with no funnel and no receipt. Every in-flight marked run is crash-parked at its deadline and, with no resumer, held for the deadline plus the TTL; after an image change the first continue usually fails park_not_restorable. Killing (5) alone while (6) is on therefore crash-parks the in-flight runs, so (6) goes off first whatever order the owner flipped them in.

F28 A crash park exists and the executor image is rolled back below S8-B: it resumes the park (S8-A code), never marks again. Rolled back below S8-A: it cannot resume (resume_incomplete); the parks are held for the crash TTL.

F29 A pinned marked run reaches a disclosure approval (cold: no pause fold exists for a pinned run) and the 'paused' tombstone is not confirmed (Unavailable after the retry): the loop STOPS before the approval exists, so no approvals row exists; the stored fold is the marked boundary fold; the run is crash-parked at the deadline and a resume re-infers and asks again. If the tombstone is confirmed the approval is raised and crash_park_run refuses the run for as long as any approvals row exists (F4). A Denied tombstone from a verifiably expired bearer with a recent heartbeat attempts the approval with the same expired bearer, which a dead bearer cannot create; if it could, the approvals fact refuses the run. If the tombstone is confirmed and then the approval cannot be created (continuation_descriptor fails, create_approval Unavailable), the loop returns Err with the 'paused' tombstone as the stored fold and no approval anywhere: the run is terminalized outcome_unknown at the deadline instead of being crash-parked (R14).

F30 session-core rolled back to an S8-A image while crash parks exist: they are spared for the PARK TTL (24 h), claimable, resumable, and no zombie fence exists beyond the seq compare-and-set; the rollback rule says drain first.

F31 A park at the credential deadline (parking and crash marking both on) is answered park_accepted false (NotAccepted): try_park closes its own row at the seq the store answered (best effort) and the writer becomes Off(SelfClosed); the loop returns the committed OutOfTime reply and writes its receipt as S8-A does. It is NOT read as a lost ownership. If the close does not land, the stray row is a typed park that finalize's terminal transition purges; the one race (replicas disagreeing about park recovery, a claimant fencing the row before the close lands) is S8-A's own exposure.

F31a The same park save is AMBIGUOUS (a timeout or a lost response). A marked loop does NOT close expected+1 and does NOT mark itself closed: the writer stays Active and the funnel's tombstone at the expected seq settles it. The park did not commit: the tombstone succeeds and the loop finalizes (a second answer is impossible without it). The park did commit: the tombstone's one probe overwrites the loop's own park and the loop proceeds. An UNCLAIMED crash park sits at that seq (the loop was superseded but alive, with a valid bearer): the tombstone is Stale and the probe takes the run back, so exactly one loop proceeds. A resume already fenced (N+2): Stale and the loop stops. A dead bearer: Denied and the age rule decides. A park that committed followed by a Denied tombstone and a stop leaves the loop's own typed credential_window park spared for the PARK TTL (24 h), resumable, with no RunParked event (the stream shows RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED). An UNMARKED loop, or an armed loop with no marked fold stored (no tombstone will settle the seq), closes expected+1 as S8-A does.

F32 A marked loop's executor is paused or partitioned past the deadline, is crash-parked, a user continues (B claims and fences), and the stalled executor wakes: its next loop top stops it by age before it can heartbeat; a save in flight at the pause is Denied or Stale and its funnel returns the stop; B is never cut off by a receipt from the old loop.

F33 A live marked loop whose end-of-round save timed out (ambiguous) is crash-parked before its next save: its probe at seq+1 can match the re-sealed seq and take the park back; if a resume had claimed but not fenced, that resume's fence is stale. One loop proceeds.

F34 Version skew: session-core's crash_reseal and execution-core's check_park_fold disagree after a change to one of them: crash parks are created and every first continue closes them (park_not_restorable); held for the crash TTL. The oracle test in S8B-2 guards one tree; the deploy order and the drain-before-rollback rule guard two.

F35 A marked loop's plan.propose or subagent.* round: the open-round pre_effect fold is saved first (only while the writer is Active). A save answered Stale, Closed or NotFound (ownership lost) holds the call; a save answered Denied dispatches it (the zombie's own bearer is dead, R13); a transient failure, or a writer that failed or is off for another reason, does NOT hold it (the call is dispatched as committed code dispatches it; a crash then parks the boundary before the call and a resume repeats it). After a successful fence a crash inside the round leaves an unmarked fold (crash_reseal refuses NotMarked), so the run is terminalized as committed; after the round's end-of-round fold the loop is marked again.

F37 The SPA follows a crash-parked run: runs.status stays running for the deadline plus the crash TTL, no run_parked frame arrives, the composer is held in its streaming state on every thread open for up to the SPA's fixed 15 minutes (a typed message is held), then 'unknown'; the only exit is Stop, which cancels the run and purges the park. Listed, not fixed here (no SPA change in S8-B).

F38 A marked loop's writer failed definitively for a non-ownership reason (Refused(KeyUnavailable | Unimplemented)) or is Off (loop_checkpoint_disabled): the funnel makes no RPC and proceeds at once (no sleep), finalize runs as committed; the visible calls are dispatched. If another replica holds the key and crash-parks the marked fold stored earlier, a superseded loop could still end the run: the drain-before-rolling rule and R19b.

F39 A marked loop whose bearers expire mid-run: with a recent last heartbeat (under 780 s) its funnel or end-of-round save answers Denied and the loop keeps the committed behaviour, an immediate failed receipt; a delegation or plan round that overruns has an unmarked stored fold, so it is never crash-parked in any case. A resume B whose bearer overran mid-round and is silent past the window stops, and its park-continue stream gets a park_continue continue_in_progress frame; 15 minutes later the run is parked again with parks+1 (the deadline again), repeatable up to the cap of 5.

F40 An UNARMED root loop (the S8B image with the switch off, or an ineligible run) reaches a loop-owned pause or a failed writer at the pause site: retire_fence returns Ok at once (its first statement is the armed check) and the approval is raised exactly as in S8-A, even when the writer already failed Stale.

F41 A degraded session-core while (5) is on: a plan or delegation round waits up to the 10 s gated timeout plus one probe before dispatch; a run end waits up to about 30 s (two tombstone attempts at the gated timeout plus one probe) and then the loop STOPS (F23); only a run that may have a marked fold stored pays this, a first-round answer makes no tombstone call. Listed with flip (5)'s effects.

F42 With (6) on and the worker missing its descriptor key: every recovered run with an active fold counts mp_session_loop_crash_park_unreadable_total{key_unavailable} (the operational family, not the refused family) and is terminalized as committed; an owner alert belongs on the unreadable family.
F36 A new user turn is appended to a thread while its run is crash-parked: the resume's answer lands after it (inherited S8-A behaviour).

F43 Session-core is restarted, deployed or recreated (flipping (6) itself is one) while (5) and (6) are on: the loop-top heartbeat maps every error to Unavailable and ends run_rounds with Err (no retry), so every loop whose loop top falls in the downtime is aborted. Each such run is a marked fold and is crash-parked at its deadline instead of ending at about 15 minutes (held up to the deadline plus the crash TTL with no resumer). Acceptable, but it belongs to the owner's flip cost list and to the choice of when to turn (6) off.

F44 The descriptor key is rotated while crash parks exist (DescriptorCipher has one key and no key id): a crash park sealed under the old key fails every claim (the executor answers resume_checkpoint_unavailable and the park is held to the crash TTL) and the worker counts did_not_authenticate for marked folds under the new key (the unreadable family). The drain query of the environment step comes first.

F45 A GDPR organization purge runs while a crash park is being re-sealed: purge_organization_data deletes run_loop_checkpoints rows before the runs rows, while the worker locks runs, obligation, fold. That lock-order inversion already exists for save and for S8-A's spare; S8-B lengthens the hold (decrypt and encrypt up to 4 MiB under three locks). The outcome is a Postgres deadlock victim, recovered by the purge's redelivery or the worker's lease; UNVERIFIED which side Postgres aborts. Not a row of data loss.

F46 Session-core lowers MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS (a faster recovery) while executors of the older image run: the executor's window is a compile-time constant, so an older executor keeps proceeding on a Denied answer for up to 780 s although a worker may act earlier. The source pin is per tree, not across deployed images: lower the executor's window first (R19f).
amendments_to_prior_specs:
AGAINST v4 (the crash-park half of s8-v4.json), each with the review finding it answers:
- THE THREAD WATERMARK and migration 0049 are DROPPED (findings 3 of rounds 1 and 2: the clock claim; round 3 critical: the claim re-check): the answer is fenced by a tombstone ordered through the fold's own seq, so nothing compares messages with the fold and nothing locks the threads row.
- loop_checkpoint_superseded, the segment comparison in save, SaveError's flag and the `loop_superseded` token are DROPPED: the executor stops on a definitive Stale, Closed or NotFound (and on Denied once its own heartbeat age is at the window, and on any unconfirmed tombstone), which the store already says, and reports with the existing closed token continue_in_progress (a new token would have needed the gateway lists, the SPA tuple, the BFF parity test and four guards for a distinction a marked loop does not need).
- fence_answer as a save of the live conversation is REPLACED by retire (a tombstone: no conversation retained, and exactly 'do not resume from here'), widened to every exit that reaches finalize (typed failures included, a gap the first draft of this design had) and to the second act nobody can take back, raising an approval.
- THE CRASH GRACE (900 s) and the heartbeat push are DROPPED: for read-only runs with a fenced exit they bought only latency. The re-seal is due at once.
- CrashFacts' ledger_after_fold with its timestamp and the release-owner check are REPLACED by two facts that use no clock: the run has no ledger row at all and no approvals row at all.
- park_crashed's list of facts is REPLACED by the pure crash_reseal shared with the executor's oracle test (round 3 critical: the marker must mean park-resumable at rest).
- EXT_PARKABLE is now computed from the allowlist the loop really runs under as well as from the request kind (round 3 suggested fix), requires a read-only run (new), and carries the identifiers in ONE payload key instead of spreading the S8-A park keys over every fold.
- The third writer_gate and the park-aware claim re-check are NOT needed and are not built.
- v4's statement that effect-capable runs are crash-parkable is REVERSED: v1 covers read-only runs only.

AGAINST S8-A AS BUILT (what S8B-1..S8B-4 change in committed S8-A code and tests):
- terminalization.rs PARK_SPARE_HORIZON_SQL gains two binds ($4 the crash TTL, $5 the reason token) and the CASE on park_reason for the wait in both places; spare_parked_run gains a fourth parameter (the crash TTL, after tx, run_id and the park TTL); PARK_HELD_SQL becomes PARK_HELD_REASON_SQL. The guards park_spare_violations and the_park_spare_follows_the_approval_spare_and_precedes_the_terminal_write pin exact strings (`WHERE run_id = $1 AND kind = 'park' AND state IN ('parked','resuming')\n        AND updated_at`, `spare_parked_run(`, `if park_recovery_active() {`): S8B-1 amends them and their mutation rows in the SAME commit (the two `$2` horizon needles, the exact-string row that removes `AND updated_at + make_interval(secs => $2) > now()` and its assert_ne!; the `if park_recovery_active() {` row needs no change and the committed rule 'the spare is called once' stays true because the crash branch runs BEFORE the single spare call), and adds the crash branch to the order they pin (after has_pending_approval, before the spare).
- durable_loop_contract park_writer_violations, run_parkable, StaticFacts (text) and park_fold are NOT changed: the marker is one new key and run_crash_parkable is an independent function, so the park-key rule, the run_parkable needles and every mutation row of the_park_writer_guard_goes_red_when_the_code_it_guards_regresses stay as committed. What changes: the StaticFacts literal in run_rounds is hoisted into a local (the builder re-verifies the guards that read it and amends only text that moved), try_park gains one note_self_closed statement (NotAccepted arm) and a conditional on its ambiguous arm's close (`!folds.is_fenced()`; the try_park rules about close_stray_park( appearing at least twice, park_fold and NotAccepted are re-verified), and OffReason gains a variant (its exhaustive match gains an arm; tests that list the reasons gain the new one).
- fold.rs Snapshot gains one field: every Snapshot literal in agent.rs (5 production sites and one test literal), park.rs's test and fold.rs's tests change (compile-driven); park_at_boundary passes None so park folds are unchanged.
- store_proofs(): the Park entry gains the S8B tests that drive the zero-retention and waived gate; switch_table(): two rows. every_guard_goes_red_when_the_code_it_guards_regresses keeps every committed row unchanged; the_park_writer_guard_goes_red_when_the_code_it_guards_regresses loses two row anchors (Site B ParkPoint and Site A max_rounds) and the_park_resume_guards_go_red_when_the_code_they_guard_regresses loses one (the `while` row), three in all, to the async block's re-indent, re-anchored whitespace-insensitively in S8B-3.
- S8-A's ledger text and failure-matrix row 19 ('the executor crashes during a park resume after the fence: ... no crash-park') are superseded when S8-B is on: that run is crash-parked again, up to the cap. S8-A's invariants 3 ('the executor never writes crash_interrupted') and 10 (the TTL) hold; invariant 10 gains 'a crash park uses the crash TTL'.
- RunDetail.park_reason can now be crash_interrupted; the SPA never reads it (run-park.ts reads the run_parked frame, which only the executor's typed parks produce) and its comment 'reserved for a later slice' becomes stale (left as is: S8-B touches no SPA file).

AGAINST THE FIVE NAMED DEFECTS, where each lives: (1) approach 3(1), crash_reseal, run_crash_parkable, tool_names_derivable, the visible-call fence, the oracle test, the crash TTL; (2) approach 2, retire_fence, the exit funnel, lost_ownership, the ordering DB test; (3) approach 3(3), the crash_park_run source scan; (4) approach 3(4) and F13/F14; (5) approach 6 and the steps' KILL ORDER and ROLLBACK paragraphs.

CLAIMS IN EARLIER TEXT THAT S8-B CORRECTS: (a) the S8 v3 and v4 designs said the worker's EXISTS on messages serializes with append_message_in_tx; it does not (append locks threads, the worker locked runs), and S8-B does not rely on it; (b) v3 named a relation tool_action_effect_ledger; it does not exist (session_tool_audit_intents does), and S8-B names the real one and uses it only as 'any row'; (c) 'a delegated subagent may never run an effectful tool' is true only of the risky list: a child can run a Write-class call (for example save_memory) that is not on it, with no fold fence and a ledger row, which is why S8-B v1 requires the read_only rung (whose gate covers every depth) rather than relying on the leaf blocklist; (d) a first draft of this design and the v4 design said a zombie is stopped by a stale fold save: a loop silent past 900 s holds session bearers that expired at 300 s, so its saves are Denied before any seq is compared, and its terminal receipt and heartbeat use fresh service tokens; S8-B treats Denied as unproven (stopped once the loop's own heartbeat age is at the window) and fences the receipt; (e) the committed heartbeat and finalize let a loop end a run that was cancelled under it: S8-B stops a MARKED loop in that case (flip (5)'s visible effect) and leaves every unmarked loop as committed.
